# Control Narrative: pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control, BR-500

**Unit:** BR-500, 2000 L single-use bioreactor (CHO culture)
**System:** DeltaV, ISA-88 batch
**Status:** DRAFT for review. Items marked **[TBD]** or **[ASSUMPTION]** need confirmation before approval.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This section defines the automatic control of culture pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) in BR-500. Each numbered requirement (e.g., PH-07) is written to be individually testable so OQ test cases can trace to it. Agitator speed is covered only where it acts as the first DO cascade stage. Temperature, pressure, and feed control are out of scope.

## 2. Instruments and Final Control Elements

| Tag | Description | Range / Limit |
|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH probes | **[TBD]** engineering range |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO probes | % air saturation |
| FCV-510 | CO₂ sparge flow control valve (acid side) | 0–2 slpm |
| P-520 | Base pump, 1 M sodium carbonate | On/off or variable **[TBD]** |
| WT-521 | Load cell, base bag | Batch base limit 40 L |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller | 80–140 rpm during DO control |
| FCV-511 | Air sparge flow control valve | 0–10 slpm |
| FCV-512 | O₂ sparge flow control valve | 0–5 slpm |

## 3. Phase Applicability

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-01 | pH and DO control shall be active only in the phases **Equilibrate, Inoculate, and Production**. |
| PH-02 | In **Media Fill** and **Harvest**, pH and DO controllers shall be inactive. FCV-510, FCV-511, FCV-512 shall be closed and P-520 stopped. SIC-530 is not driven by the DO cascade. |
| PH-03 | On entry to an active phase, controllers shall start in automatic mode with the setpoints defined in the recipe. Transition between active phases shall be bumpless (no output reset or setpoint step). |
| PH-04 | On phase transition to an inactive phase, the outputs in PH-02 shall be applied. |
| PH-05 | On Hold, Abort, or Stop of the batch, the outputs shall go to the state defined in the phase failure handling **[TBD: confirm safe state, including whether agitation and minimum gas flow are maintained]**. |

## 4. pH Control

### 4.1 Measurement and probe selection

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-10 | The pH process value (PV) shall be the arithmetic mean of AT-501A and AT-501B when both are healthy. |
| PH-11 | A probe is unhealthy if its signal is bad quality, out of range, or open/short circuit. It is also unhealthy if marked failed by the operator **[TBD: any additional diagnostics]**. |
| PH-12 | If one probe is unhealthy, the PV shall be the healthy probe only, and an alarm identifying the failed probe shall be raised. Control continues. |
| PH-13 | If both probes are unhealthy, control shall go to a safe state: CO₂ valve closed and P-520 stopped. A high-priority alarm shall be raised. The batch shall be placed in Hold **[ASSUMPTION; confirm]**. |
| PH-14 | If both probes are healthy and differ by more than **[TBD]** pH units for more than **[TBD]** s, a probe deviation alarm shall be raised. Control continues on the average **[ASSUMPTION; alternative is to require operator selection]**. |
| PH-15 | Return to the averaged PV after a probe recovers shall require operator acknowledgment **[ASSUMPTION]**, and shall be bumpless. |

### 4.2 Setpoint, deadband, and actuation

Setpoint (SP) = 7.00. Deadband = 0.05 **[ASSUMPTION: interpreted as ±0.05 around SP, so the neutral zone is 6.95–7.05]**.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-20 | The pH SP shall be 7.00 (recipe parameter). |
| PH-21 | **Acid side:** When PV > SP + 0.05, FCV-510 shall modulate within 0–2 slpm to reduce PV. Control action is PID **[TBD: tuning, or proportional to error]**. |
| PH-22 | CO₂ flow shall return to 0 slpm when PV falls to or below SP **[ASSUMPTION: confirm return threshold and any hysteresis]**. |
| PH-23 | **Base side:** When PV < SP − 0.05, P-520 shall dose 1 M sodium carbonate to raise PV. Dosing pattern (continuous or pulsed, pulse size, minimum off time) **[TBD]**. |
| PH-24 | Base dosing shall stop when PV returns to or above SP **[ASSUMPTION]**. |
| PH-25 | Acid and base actions shall be mutually exclusive. P-520 shall not run while FCV-510 is open, and vice versa. |
| PH-26 | FCV-510 output shall be clamped to 0–2 slpm. Output shall not exceed 2 slpm under any condition. |

### 4.3 Base addition limit

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-30 | The total base added per batch shall be calculated from the weight loss of the base bag measured by WT-521, converted to volume using a configured density **[TBD: density value and its source]**. |
| PH-31 | The cumulative total shall be initialized at batch start, shall persist through Hold/Restart, and shall not be reset by the operator during the batch. |
| PH-32 | A warning alarm shall be raised when the total reaches **[TBD]** L (suggest 80% = 32 L). |
| PH-33 | When the total reaches **40 L**, P-520 shall be stopped, locked out for the remainder of the batch, and a high-priority alarm raised. Acid-side control shall remain active. |
| PH-34 | Clearing the P-520 lockout shall not be possible from the operator interface. Override requires **[TBD: a deviation process / authorized role]**. |
| PH-35 | If WT-521 is bad quality, the base total cannot be verified. The system shall raise an alarm and **[TBD: stop P-520 (conservative), or estimate from pump run time]**. |
| PH-36 | Replacing or refilling the base bag shall not corrupt the total **[TBD: define how a bag swap is handled]**. |

## 5. DO Control

### 5.1 Measurement and probe selection

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-01 | The DO PV shall be the mean of AT-502A and AT-502B when both are healthy. |
| DO-02 | If one probe is unhealthy, the PV shall be the healthy probe only, with an alarm. If both are unhealthy, the cascade shall go to the safe state in DO-30 with a high-priority alarm. |
| DO-03 | A probe deviation alarm shall be raised at a difference > **[TBD]** % for > **[TBD]** s. |
| DO-04 | Probe health and recovery rules shall be identical in form to PH-11 and PH-15. |

### 5.2 Setpoint and cascade

The DO SP is 40% air saturation. The DO controller output is allocated sequentially across three actuators.

| Stage | Actuator | Range | Engages when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SIC-530 agitator | 80 → 140 rpm | Demand rises above the baseline |
| 2 | FCV-511 air sparge | 0 → 10 slpm | SIC-530 is at 140 rpm and demand continues |
| 3 | FCV-512 O₂ sparge | 0 → 5 slpm | FCV-511 is at 10 slpm and demand continues |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-10 | The DO SP shall be 40% air saturation (recipe parameter). |
| DO-11 | When DO PV < SP, demand shall be met first by increasing SIC-530 from 80 to 140 rpm. FCV-511 and FCV-512 shall not increase above their baseline until SIC-530 is at 140 rpm. |
| DO-12 | Only when SIC-530 is at 140 rpm shall FCV-511 increase from 0 toward 10 slpm. FCV-512 shall not increase until FCV-511 is at 10 slpm. |
| DO-13 | Only when FCV-511 is at 10 slpm shall FCV-512 increase from 0 toward 5 slpm. |
| DO-14 | When demand falls, the cascade shall unwind in reverse order: FCV-512 to 0, then FCV-511 to 0, then SIC-530 back toward 80 rpm. |
| DO-15 | Agitator speed shall be no lower than 80 rpm and no higher than 140 rpm while DO control is active. Air shall not exceed 10 slpm and O₂ shall not exceed 5 slpm. |
| DO-16 | Stage transitions shall be bumpless and shall not chatter. Transition hysteresis/overlap **[TBD]**. |
| DO-17 | When DO PV > SP, stages shall unwind as in DO-14, subject to the minimum values in DO-15. Whether a baseline air flow is maintained at the lowest cascade stage **[TBD]**. |
| DO-18 | DO PID tuning (gains, integral time, anti-windup on stage saturation) **[TBD]**. |

### 5.3 DO limits and failure handling

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-20 | Low and high DO alarms at **[TBD]** % and **[TBD]** % with on-delay **[TBD]**. |
| DO-21 | An alarm shall be raised if the cascade is fully saturated (all stages at maximum) and DO remains below SP − **[TBD]** % for > **[TBD]** min. |
| DO-30 | With both DO probes unhealthy, the cascade shall freeze at the last values for **[TBD]** min then move to a defined safe state **[TBD]**, with a high-priority alarm. |

## 6. Interaction Between pH and DO

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| IX-01 | CO₂ added for pH and gas added for DO shall each be controlled by its own loop. No cross-compensation is applied **[ASSUMPTION; confirm any limit on total gas flow or headspace pressure]**. |
| IX-02 | Total sparge flow limits (if any) **[TBD]**. |

## 7. Setpoint Change Recording (QA Requirement)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SP-01 | During the **Production** phase, any change to the pH SP or DO SP shall require the operator to enter a reason before the change takes effect. |
| SP-02 | The entry shall record: tag/parameter, old value, new value, date/time, user ID, and reason text. |
| SP-03 | If no reason is entered, or the entry is cancelled, the setpoint shall remain unchanged. |
| SP-04 | The record shall be stored in the electronic batch record / event journal, shall be attributable and time-stamped, and shall not be editable or deletable by operators. |
| SP-05 | The recorded entry shall be retrievable in the batch report. |
| SP-06 | **[TBD]** Whether the same applies to deadband changes, cascade limits, and tuning parameters. We recommend it does. Changes outside Production should still be logged, but without mandatory reason entry unless QA requires it. |
| SP-07 | **[TBD]** Role-based permission to change the setpoints (which user roles). |
| SP-08 | Setpoint changes made by recipe at phase transition (not by an operator) shall be logged as recipe-driven. |

## 8. Alarm Summary

| Alarm | Trigger | Priority | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH probe failure (single) | PH-12 | Medium | Continue on healthy probe |
| pH probe failure (both) | PH-13 | High | Safe state, Hold |
| pH probe deviation | PH-14 | Medium | Operator investigation |
| pH high / low | **[TBD]** | **[TBD]** | None automatic |
| Base total warning | PH-32 | Medium | Notify |
| Base limit reached | PH-33 | High | P-520 lockout |
| WT-521 failure | PH-35 | High | Per PH-35 |
| DO probe failure / deviation | DO-02, DO-03 | Medium/High | Per requirement |
| DO high / low | DO-20 | **[TBD]** | None automatic |
| Cascade saturated | DO-21 | High | Notify |

## 9. OQ Test Derivation Guidance

Each requirement maps to at least one test. Suggested test types:

- **Phase gating (PH-01 to PH-05):** Run through each phase and verify that outputs are active or closed as specified. Verify behavior on Hold/Abort.
- **Probe handling (PH-10 to PH-15, DO-01 to DO-04):** Simulate each probe fault, both faults, a deviation condition, and recovery.
- **pH actuation (PH-20 to PH-26):** Drive the PV across ±0.05 thresholds. Verify acid/base action, mutual exclusion, and the 2 slpm clamp.
- **Base limit (PH-30 to PH-36):** Simulate bag weight loss to the warning threshold and to 40 L. Verify lockout, non-resettability by an operator, persistence through Hold, and load cell failure.
- **DO cascade (DO-10 to DO-18):** Step the DO PV below and above SP. Verify the stage order, boundary values (80/140 rpm, 10 slpm, 5 slpm), reverse unwinding, and bumpless transitions.
- **DO failure (DO-20 to DO-30):** Simulate saturation and loss of both probes.
- **Setpoint changes (SP-01 to SP-08):** Change SP in Production with a reason, without a reason, and by cancelling. Verify audit contents and immutability. Verify the behavior in non-Production phases.

## 10. Open Items for Resolution

1. Deadband interpretation and return thresholds (PH-22, PH-24).
2. Base pump type and dosing logic; base density for the 40 L calculation.
3. Behavior on load cell failure and on bag change.
4. Safe states for Hold/Abort and for loss of both probes.
5. All alarm limits, delays, and probe deviation thresholds.
6. PID tuning and cascade hysteresis; baseline air flow.
7. Scope of audited parameters beyond the two setpoints, and role permissions.
8. Whether the 40 L limit override is permitted, and by whom.
